transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-03
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Jon Ramos (Redwood); Evelyn Park, Omar Ruiz, Priya Sethi, Noah Kim (LatticeCore)

Summary (auto): exploratory partner sync; not a demo.

00:00 Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Maya, I'm the AE for the West region at Redwood. With me is Jon, our systems engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:07 Evelyn (LatticeCore): Hi Maya — good, thanks. Excited to talk through how we might partner.
00:10 Omar: hey, yeah, morning all. we've been looking at options for GPU onramp for our customers.
00:18 Maya: Great. Quick agenda — we want to understand your business model, constraints (network, security), what you see as the ideal integration (reseller, co-managed, or straight referral), and then tech constraints. We'll follow with next steps. Sound okay?
00:29 Priya: sounds good. we're mostly interested in a channel where we can offer managed GPU capacity to enterprise clients, and potentially run Redwood Dedicated behind our VPC for customers that need isolation.
00:40 Jon (Redwood SE): quick clarifying q: when you say "managed GPU capacity" is that a hosted tenancy on your infra where you run inference for your customers, or are you thinking of reselling Redwood Dedicated instances?
00:50 Priya: a bit of both — some customers will want us to fully operate inference, others will want a dedicated contract with Redwood but fronted through LatticeCore for billing and support.
01:02 Maya: got it. so licensing and billing model flexibility is important. On the tech side, can you sketch the network topology and typical egress patterns? any shared peering concerns?
01:13 Omar: yeah — our default is VPC peering to partner endpoints, with private link options. shared peering is doable but some customers disallow cross-VPC traffic, so we need on-prem or private deploy options.
01:26 Jon: okay that's helpful. Redwood Private supports a VPC-managed control plane and an optional on-prem bundle for air-gapped/regulated customers. Our runtime is flexible; we can collocate with you or run in your cloud account.
01:36 Noah: the compliance part is big too — SOC2 is a must for our enterprise customers; flight logs, audit trails, SSO, KMS integration — we need to see docs.
01:47 Maya: understood. we have a security packet — SOC2, ISO notes, KMS integrations, SAML/SCIM for SSO and RBAC controls. I'll share that.
01:55 Evelyn: with the Dedicated offering, what are typical throughput numbers for a 2-GPU pool? average TPS for chat and for embeddings? rough order of magnitude is fine.
02:06 Jon: rough numbers, ballpark: small models (embedding-ish) you might see hundreds of requests per second with batching, but chat workloads are more token-limited. For a 2xA10/RTX style pool you'd be looking at X to Y rps depending on sequence length. (note: numbers fuzzy in transcript)
02:22 Priya: ok, can you give an example of how batching would affect latency? some of our customers cannot accept >300ms tail latencies.
02:31 Jon: important note — batching helps throughput but increases tail latencies; Redwood Optimize can suggest batching configs and prefix-cache to help keep p95 down. For the strict 300ms SLO you may need more compute headroom or smaller batch windows.
02:48 Maya: Are you planning to run heavy quantized models or MLaaS style? Also curious what models you expect customers to use — open weights, or proprietary?
02:58 Evelyn: most customers are leaning towards open models, but they're starting to bring private finetuned models. So we need secure model custody and maybe per-tenant KV cache isolation.
03:09 Jon: we support model pinning and rollout policies; per-tenant isolation for KV cache is doable, and our private deployment can encrypt models at rest with KMS.
03:20 Omar: network egress — if we colocate with LatticeCore infra, what's the bandwidth needed? and is there an upstream dependency to Redwood control plane?
03:29 Jon: control plane chatter is minimal; inference traffic stays local if deployed in your region/account. For bandwidth, it depends on tokens and payloads — bulk embeddings are heavier. We'll follow up with a perf sheet.
03:42 Evelyn: commercial question — do you allow reseller marks and flexible pricing? we need margin to sell.
03:49 Maya: Redwood has partner pricing tiers; we can align on reseller discounts for committed capacity. Dedicated contracts can be reseller-enabled under partner agreement. I'll add a stub in the partner brief.
03:59 Priya: one blocker: some verticals need air-gapped deployments — can Redwood run an offline private control plane?
04:08 Jon: yes, on-prem package supports an air-gapped deployment but it takes more setup and a different support SLA. we'll outline the steps in a tech-dive.
04:20 Noah: curious — any limits on model size? some customers want to run 70B or larger.
04:25 Jon: runtime supports large models; you need the right GPU class and kernel selection. For 70B, you typically want multi-GPU NVLink or sharded execution — we can recommend target instantiation.
04:38 Maya: Competitive landscape — have you evaluated NGC or other partners?
04:41 Evelyn: yes, NVIDIA NGC and Run:ai were on the shortlist. Pain points with those were heavy ops burden or opaque pricing.
04:51 Maya: That's helpful. Redwood positions around predictable ops and transparent perf/cost.
04:57 Omar: network security — do you support customer-managed KMS?
05:02 Jon: yes, customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported in Private installs; logs and audit trails can be integrated with your SIEM.
05:12 Priya: what about latency monitoring and SLA? we need per-tenant traces and tracing hooks into our observability stack.
05:20 Jon: Console exports tracing hooks and token-level cost/latency breakdowns; we can forward traces to your datadog/blackbox setup.
05:29 Maya: quick note on onboarding: for a pilot we usually recommend a small Dedicated pool with a 4-week test, shared runbook, and a small benchmark for the top 2 workloads. That pilot can be co-sold.
05:44 Evelyn: sounds reasonable. our initial pilot customers will be fintech and healthtech where compliance matters.
05:51 Maya: understood. Any immediate red flags?
05:54 Omar: only one — licensing/recourse if a customer needs full data deletion or key escrow — we need clear language.
06:02 Maya: we'll include terms and an escalation path in the partner packet.
06:08 Priya: another technical ask — can we get a matrix for quantization profiles vs model families? Some customers demand performance comparers for int8 vs fp16.
06:17 Jon: yes, Jon will prepare a quantization/throughput matrix for the common open families.
06:23 Evelyn: timeline-wise, we're looking to pilot with customers in July. Is that realistic?
06:28 Maya: tight but doable if we get topology and expected load by mid-June and run a pilot config in late June.
06:36 Noah: ok let's aim for July pilots.
06:39 Maya: Excellent. I'll send the partner brief and security packet. Jon will follow up with technical doc and perf numbers. We'll schedule the deeper tech-run in week of June 15.
06:51 Evelyn: thanks everyone.
06:53 Maya: quick recap of next steps... (recap items listed)
06:59 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: some numeric perf figures were verbal approximations; recommend following up for exact benchmark values. Links shared: partner one-pager (link placeholder), security packet (link placeholder), perf spreadsheet (link placeholder).
